A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same APOLLO framework and provide readable text, tables, figures, and proof examples. v1 ends after its references; v3 adds Appendices A-C, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1-2 and Figures 3-5 report original APOLLO experiments on miniF2F-test, including accuracy, sampling costs, proof-length distributions, and recursion-depth effects.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds Goedel-V2 comparisons, token-cost results, and detailed proof-repair outcomes in Appendices B-C.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Syntax Refiner, Sorrifier, Auto Solver, recursive sub-lemma repair, and Proof Assembler. Appendix A documents these components more precisely through pseudocode and implementation details, without establishing a change to the underlying procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Lean4 theorem proving on the same 244-problem miniF2F-test partition. The additional model and appendix examples remain within this benchmark and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Goedel-V2, an 8B whole-proof generator, with baseline results at sampling budgets 32, 64, and 128 and a paired APOLLO comparison. Existing comparison methods are retained, including those whose names are abbreviated in v3.

E3.justification: v3 adds average generated-token expenditure as an evaluation metric and introduces settings for the Goedel-V2 comparison. Section 4.4 and Figure 5 extend the reported Goedel-Prover-SFT and Kimina recursion-depth sweeps from 0-5 to 0-6. The benchmark split, Lean version, and stated sub-proof sampling setting remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices B-C substantially expand the diagnostic case studies beyond v1's Figure 2 illustration. Figure 6 traces six failing sub-lemmas through solver assistance and recursion; Figures 7-16 examine solver-only repairs, redundant-tactic removal, missing intermediate lemmas, and deeper recursive repairs. The original proof-length analysis remains, while the recursion-depth analysis gains depth-6 observations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark accuracy. The retained violin plots describe variation across proof lengths, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive token-cost results and Goedel-V2 outcomes: APOLLO reaches 84.9% at 63 samples and 344K tokens, while the base model reaches 84.9% at 128 samples and 699K tokens. Original headline accuracies of 65.6% for Goedel-Prover-SFT and 75.0% for Kimina remain unchanged. Table 2 corrects o3-mini's reported gain from 33.2 to 36.9 percentage points without changing its 40.2% accuracy. Depth-6 and appendix repair outcomes are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Beyond the retained Figure 2 example, Appendices B-C add explicit mathematical statements and worked Lean proof derivations for further benchmark problems. This expands the documented mathematical proof examples, while adding no general theoretical guarantees or analytical results about APOLLO.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the 75.0% headline among 7B models with fewer than 1,000 samples by 84.9% among 'sub 8B' models with fewer than 100 samples. The conclusion expands the evaluated model count from four to five. The central contribution remains model-agnostic, compiler-guided proof repair with improved sampling efficiency.

C2.justification: The appendices add specific explanations of why removing redundant tactics can complete a proof, why broad solver tactics sometimes require additional auxiliary lemmas, and how explicit type information protects extracted goals. The existing limitations concerning poor initial proof sketches and untested integration with tree-search methods remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly supplies APOLLO code-access information and substantial implementation documentation in Appendix A: recursive pseudocode, regex-based syntax repairs, malformed-statement handling, explicit Lean type-printing options, and filtering of hint suggestions. These operational disclosures substantially exceed v1's higher-level module descriptions and retained hardware settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Goedel-Prover-V2 reference and positions that model as a current state-of-the-art comparator in Section 4.2. The related-work discussion and other cited works remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and nearly all introductory, related-work, methodological, and limitations prose are retained. Edits update the abstract and conclusion, add an author and an appendix cross-reference, and organize the additional explanations into Appendices A-C.

P2.justification: Figure 3 expands from two sampling-budget panels to four panels including token budgets. Tables 1-2 gain token columns, Table 1 replaces APOLLO's sample-count column with recursion depth, and Figure 4 is enlarged and rearranged. Figure 5 extends its depth axes, while Algorithm 1 and Figures 6-16 add substantial new visual documentation.

improvement.justification: Token-cost comparisons, implementation details, code-access information, and worked repair cases make APOLLO's efficiency and operation easier to assess than in v1. The Goedel-V2 experiment adds useful supporting evidence. However, the new 84.9% state-of-the-art headline overstates Table 2, which shows APOLLO matching the base model's peak accuracy at lower cost; the abstract's 'sub 8B' wording also conflicts with the listed 8B model. The added transparency and evidence provide a net improvement, tempered by these reporting inconsistencies.
